title: Python SDK ergonomic streaming chat event iterator + checkpointing API
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Problem: Users integrating streaming chat completions commonly need: an easy-to-use iterator abstraction that yields high-level events (tokens, deltas, function calls, done), robust resume/checkpoint semantics for intermittent client/network failures, clear backpressure semantics for sync + async usage, and a predictable retry model for idempotent requests. Current SDK prototypes expose raw event websockets/callbacks that force application authors to reimplement checkpointing and retry glue.
proposal_summary: Introduce a first-class StreamingEventIterator with explicit checkpoint() and resume(checkpoint_token) APIs, consistent sync/async iterator ergonomics, built-in at-least-once vs at-most-once semantics opt-in, and a small event middleware hook for logging/metrics and filtering. Provide pattern-based examples for 1) low-latency interactive UIs, 2) batch consumer with durable checkpointing, and 3) server-side replay with idempotency tokens.
design_decisions: 1) Single iterator type for sync + async: keep API consistent; separate constructors stream_sync() and stream_async() to avoid runtime checks. 2) Checkpoint token is opaque string signed by Redwood to include (request_id, offset_in_tokens, model_variant). Developers must not parse it. 3) Retry model defaults to at-least-once with dedupe via idempotency_key; optional strict at-most-once if user provides durable checkpoint storage. 4) Backpressure: iterator.pop() should block for new events in sync mode and await in async; users can supply max_buffer_size to control memory. 5) Middleware: simple list of callables run for each event; cannot mutate token streams but can add tags/metrics. 6) Streaming errors: fatal errors surface via iterator exception; transient network errors trigger automatic reconnect using exponential backoff and resume if checkpoint is available.
acceptance_criteria:
- Python SDK exposes StreamingEventIterator with clear constructor docs and type hints.
- API supports iterator.checkpoint() -> str and static method StreamingEventIterator.resume(checkpoint: str) to continue.
- Both sync and async usage examples in README and examples/ folder.
- Integration tests covering: reconnect+resume, buffer overflow handling, idempotency with duplicate events, middleware invocation.
- End-to-end demo app (notebook) shows user resuming a 10-minute streaming session after simulated network loss.
- Documentation page in docs.redwood.ai with example code snippets and migration guide.
- Performance regression: library overhead <3% p99 vs current raw socket prototype under 100rps benchmark.

risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Checkpoint token becomes a compatibility footgun if format changes. Mitigation: make token opaque and include version header; provide server-side mapping for old tokens.
Risk: Users rely on strict at-most-once; our default at-least-once could surprise. Mitigation: document default clearly and add explicit 'mode' parameter.
Risk: Buffering large messages leads to OOM in sync consumers. Mitigation: enforce configurable max_buffer_size and provide streaming 'drain' callbacks.

comments: 2026-02-11 Diego Martinez: Spiked a sync iterator prototype that yields Event(token=..., type='delta') objects. Using a single class with __iter__ and __aiter__ felt brittle; moved to explicit constructors stream_sync()/stream_async().

2026-02-18 Priya Nair: Implemented checkpoint encoding with version header 'v1|' + base64 payload. Need security review to ensure token can't be forged. Added unit tests for encoding/decoding. https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/1289/files

2026-02-24 Marco Alvarez: Added middleware hook signatures; opted for (event, context) -> Optional[event] so filters can drop events. Decided to not allow mutation of token contents to avoid subtle consistency bugs.

2026-03-02 QA Bot: Integration test failure when simulating flaky TLS connection — reconnect logic retried too aggressively causing server rate-limit. Lowered reconnect attempts and added jitter. CI: https://ci.redwood.ai/blue/organizations/jenkins/sdk-python/detail/PR-1289/5/pipeline
2026-03-07 Alyssa Chen: Docs draft uploaded to docs repo and example notebooks updated. Need feedback from DX on wording for migration guide. https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/python/streaming-events

2026-03-10 Security: Reviewed checkpoint token design; OK to proceed if tokens are HMAC-signed and short TTL applied. Added requirement to rotate signing keys and log validation failures. (security ticket SEC-214)
2026-03-12 Diego Martinez: Running perf comparisons vs raw socket prototype. Overhead at p99 is ~1.9% for iterator wrapping; acceptable. Scheduling rollout to beta testers next week.
